attacks.claim: Reverting to 4.7 or turning Away Assist off does not say what happens to a unit already in Away mode. Since 4.7 has no Away Assist logic, the unit could stay in Away at the Away setpoints with no motion-based return.
attacks.evidence: "Revert: push 4.7 to updated units through the same OTA path; schedules fall back to their v1 copy and Away Assist turns off (Home/Away history is deleted)." ABSENT: whether the unit leaves Away and returns to schedule on revert.

attacks.claim: Away Assist can set heating to Away after 2 h without motion during home periods. A still or sleeping occupant the wall-mounted sensor cannot see gets set back with no visible cause. The artifact describes no freeze floor or mitigation for Away setpoints during present occupancy.
attacks.evidence: "sets Away mode after 2 h with no motion during scheduled 'home' periods... Away uses the user's existing Away setpoints." / "freeze/heat protection is never interrupted" (stated only for install deferral)

attacks.claim: The schedule downgrade is lossy and cannot be undone. v2 is collapsed to 4 periods on every edit, and a 4.7 edit makes the cloud discard v2, so a later re-upgrade cannot restore the 8-period schedule. The 'simplified' notice appears only in the app, so a unit that is not opened in the app gets no notice.
attacks.evidence: "When a unit on 4.7 edits its schedule, the cloud discards the stale v2 copy, so a later re-upgrade starts from the current v1 schedule." / "The app shows 'Some schedule changes were simplified' if v2 had more than 4 periods."

attacks.claim: Automatic revert covers only boot and self-test failures. A 4.8 image that boots but misbehaves in HVAC control has no automatic revert. The only recovery is a manual OTA push, which depends on the same single OTA service that the halt uses.
attacks.evidence: "If 4.8 fails to boot or fails its post-boot self-test 3 times, the unit reverts to 4.7 automatically." / "Revert: push 4.7 to updated units through the same OTA path" / "Halt: pause the OTA campaign (one switch)"

attacks.claim: The revert is tested on only 300 qa-fleet units, but the fleet is 612k units across three hardware revs and multiple HVAC types. Revert time is also unbounded: units install only in a 02:00-05:00 window, only with no active HVAC call, only at 7-32 °C, and users can postpone up to 14 days. None of these constraints are shown to work at fleet scale.
attacks.evidence: "Tested on 300 `qa-fleet` units." / "Install window 02:00-05:00 local; the unit waits until no HVAC call is active." / "Users can postpone an update up to 14 days from the app."

attacks.claim: The install window has no timeout, fallback window, or retry rule. In heating season a unit may never see an idle HVAC period between 02:00 and 05:00 and could defer indefinitely. Stage gates count only updated units, so this skews them.
attacks.evidence: "Install window 02:00-05:00 local; the unit waits until no HVAC call is active." ABSENT: timeout or retry behavior.

attacks.claim: The freeze/heat protection guarantee conflicts with the design. Relays are deliberately off for the ~90 s install, and the failed-boot retry path (3 attempts before revert) has no stated bound on relay-off duration.
attacks.evidence: "During the ~90 s install, relays are held open (off)." / "so freeze/heat protection is never interrupted." ABSENT: relay state and duration during boot-failure retries.

attacks.claim: The HIL bench explicitly excludes no-C-wire power-stealing configurations. Relay behavior during the 90 s install and the post-install reboot in those configurations is unproven, yet the artifact relies on relays being held safely open.
attacks.evidence: "HIL bench: conventional 1H/1C, 2-stage, heat pump + aux, no C-wire power stealing; rev B/C/D | Pass, 0 relay faults over 72 h"

attacks.claim: Stage 1 gate is statistically underpowered. At ~6,100 units, 0.05% is about 3 events, so one or two failures can halt the rollout and zero events can pass it. Gate criteria count only updated units, and postponement or install windows mean few units may update within 3 days.
attacks.evidence: "Stage 1 | 1% (~6,100) | 3 days | boot-revert rate < 0.05%" / "Users can postpone an update up to 14 days from the app." ABSENT: sample-size or detection-power justification.

attacks.claim: Stage 4 moves from 50% to 100% (~306k units) with no duration, soak, or advance criteria.

Gate and paging criteria are not reconciled. The stage gate uses 0.05% over 3-4 day stages, while paging uses 0.1% over 6 h windows. No action is defined for a gate breach except a manual halt, and what on-call does when paged is not stated.
attacks.evidence: "boot-revert rate < 0.05%" (advance) vs. "boot reverts exceed 0.1% of updated units in any 6 h window" (page)

attacks.claim: Monitoring does not cover stuck or incomplete installs. A unit that stalls with relays held off during the 90 s install, or stays offline after a halt or revert, may not trigger any page under the stated rules. The artifact also does not say what happens to units mid-install when a halt or revert is pushed.
attacks.evidence: "Pages firmware on-call if boot reverts exceed 0.1% of updated units in any 6 h window or offline rate rises 0.5 points over baseline." / "Halt: pause the OTA campaign (one switch); units not yet updated stay on 4.7."

attacks.claim: The halt mechanism is a stated gate requirement and stage advancement depends on it, but no QA row tests pausing the campaign.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: QA row for halt. "Halt: pause the OTA campaign (one switch)" has no test reference.

attacks.claim: The schedule re-upgrade path is asserted but untested. The QA covers 4.8-edit then downgrade, not a 4.7 edit followed by re-upgrade to 4.8, and not a unit that is offline during the 4.7 edit.
attacks.evidence: "so a later re-upgrade starts from the current v1 schedule." vs QA: "v1/v2 schedule: edit on 4.8, downgrade to 4.7 via OTA, schedule present and correct | Pass"

attacks.claim: The privacy claims that raw motion stays on-device, that Home/Away state is absent from the partner API, and that Home/Away data is deleted after 7 days have no verification evidence. Home/Away events also flow into telemetry ingest, and the artifact does not say whether that copy follows the same 7-day deletion.
attacks.evidence: "No raw motion data leaves the thermostat." / "Home/Away state is not exposed through the partner integrations API." / "Home/Away state adds ~1 small event per state change" to telemetry ingest. ABSENT: network capture, API test, or retention test.

attacks.claim: The deletion guarantee holds only for the device toggle. A forced revert across 612k units is not shown to delete Home/Away data from cloud copies, backups, or telemetry.
attacks.evidence: "Revert: ... Away Assist turns off (Home/Away history is deleted)." / "Turning it off deletes stored Home/Away history." ABSENT: deletion scope beyond the device-initiated toggle.

attacks.claim: Cloud-stored Home/Away occupancy history has no described access control. The artifact asserts it is not exposed through partner APIs but does not say who or what can read the 7-day store.
attacks.evidence: "Only the resulting Home/Away state is sent to the cloud... kept 7 days" / ABSENT: access-control description for the Home/Away store.

attacks.claim: A new cloud-stored personal data type, Home/Away state for US and Canadian homes, has no hosting region or jurisdiction stated. Residency and cross-border handling are unverified.
attacks.evidence: "Only the resulting Home/Away state is sent to the cloud (needed to show it in the app); it is kept 7 days and then deleted." ABSENT: hosting region or data residency statement.

attacks.claim: Away Assist creates a new information system holding occupancy-derived personal information about people in Canada. No privacy impact assessment reference is given. Confirm whether a PIA is required under Quebec Law 25 before crossing.
attacks.evidence: "Privacy notice section 3 updated (legal review LGL-4471)." ABSENT: PIA reference for the Home/Away system.

attacks.claim: The v1 derivation (keep the 4 periods closest to anchors) has no stated spec for ties, missing anchors, or overlapping periods. The QA only checks that the schedule is 'present and correct', so the behavior is hard to test.
attacks.evidence: "keeping the 4 periods closest to the user's wake / leave / return / sleep anchors" / QA: "schedule present and correct"

attacks.claim: The no-motion timer's behavior at schedule boundaries is undefined. It is unclear whether the 2 h counter resets or carries across home periods.
attacks.evidence: "after 2 h with no motion during scheduled 'home' periods" with no boundary or reset rule.

attacks.claim: The absolute claim 'reconnect < 60 s' rests on a p99 of 41 s over 500 reboots. The maximum and tail variance are not reported, so some reconnects could exceed 60 s.
attacks.evidence: "Wi-Fi reconnect after router reboot now < 60 s." vs "reconnect p99 41 s over 500 reboots"

attacks.claim: The 6% energy claim is from a 2025-26 trial, but the artifact does not state which firmware or Away Assist build the trial ran. It also measures heating runtime, not bills or comfort, so consumers may read it as a savings promise.
attacks.evidence: "In our 2025-26 field trial of 412 homes, Away Assist cut heating runtime by a median of 6%." No build or firmware version stated.

attacks.claim: The temperature deferral is tested only at the 5 °C bound. The 32 °C upper bound and the post-boot self-test failure path have no test rows.
attacks.evidence: "Temperature deferral at 5 °C chamber test | Pass" / "fails its post-boot self-test" has no injection row.

attacks.claim: New user-facing text and UI have no test evidence. The 9.2 'Update the app' prompt and the 'simplified' notice have no assistive-technology or French check. Contrast, reduced-motion, and on-device Away/schedule indication are not described.
attacks.evidence: "App 9.3 schedule editor and Away Assist screens with VoiceOver, TalkBack, 200% text | Pass" / ABSENT: contrast, reduce-motion, and on-device display checks.

attacks.claim: Signing key custody and channel separation are not described. Testing used the production-signed image on the qa-fleet channel, so controls that keep qa-channel or unsigned images from reaching the public fleet are not stated.
attacks.evidence: "production-signed 4.8 image delivered through the production OTA service on the `qa-fleet` channel" / ABSENT: key custody and channel-scoping controls.

attacks.claim: The anti-rollback design keeps 4.7 installable only for this release. Nothing records a constraint that future releases keep 4.7 installable, so a later counter increment could close the revert path this rollout depends on.
attacks.evidence: "4.8 does not increment the secure-boot anti-rollback counter (no security fixes in this release), so 4.7 remains installable."

attacks.claim: All firmware distribution (~1.5 TB) runs through one CDN contract with no secondary origin, so a CDN outage would block updates and rollbacks fleet-wide.
attacks.evidence: "OTA egress: 2.4 MB image × 612k units ≈ 1.5 TB via existing CDN contract, within the monthly commit." ABSENT: secondary CDN or origin.

attacks.claim: The +0.4% telemetry projection has no bound on state-change frequency. Motion flapping around the 2 h threshold could exceed it. The 1.5 TB egress also omits retries, resumes, and the rollback egress.
attacks.evidence: "Home/Away state adds ~1 small event per state change; projected +0.4% on telemetry ingest." / "Revert: push 4.7 to updated units through the same OTA path"

attacks.claim: Unrelated fixes (humidity drift and Wi-Fi reconnect) ship in the same release as the schedule format change and Away Assist. This widens the blast radius and makes it harder to attribute or roll back one change.
attacks.evidence: "Fixes: humidity reading drift on rev B boards; Wi-Fi reconnect after router reboot now < 60 s."
